output.summary: KEP-4601 proposed extending authorization attributes with field and label selectors from List, Watch, and DeleteCollection so authorizers (webhook, SAR/SSAR, node, CEL) can use them in decisions. Status is implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: Per-node workloads need tighter security, and out-of-tree authorizers need selector information to express restrictions. The design exposes selectors as authorization attributes without adding an in-tree selector-managing authorizer or expanding audit and admission surfaces. Reviewers settled that selector requirements are ANDed server-side, so unrecognized operators can be treated safely, and that selector parse failures and unsupported verbs should error rather than silently drop the selector.

alternatives.option: Add a second, separate parsed-requirements representation alongside the raw selector string in the SAR body
alternatives.why_not: Reviewer luxas objected to the sprawl of two near-identical representations and wanted a canonical codec library instead.

alternatives.option: Drop unparseable or unsupported selectors as non-limiting, as the SubjectAccessReview API does
alternatives.why_not: deads2k said leniency makes it hard to discover VAP or binding bugs, so the design errors instead; the author updated the KEP accordingly.

alternatives.option: Use a separate optional interface for selector access instead of adding methods to authorizer.Attributes
alternatives.why_not: luxas disliked this option; deads2k accepted breaking implementers of the interface as an explicit way to force the semantic change.

alternatives.option: Change selector combination from AND to another semantic
alternatives.why_not: liggitt argued AND lets webhooks short-circuit on known limits and safely ignore unknown operators, so changing it would break future operator expansion.

evidence.quote: The authorization attributes will be extended to include field selectors and label selectors from List, Watch, and DeleteCollection.
Currently every discrete requirement is AND'd when evaluated server-side. I don't see a need to change that behavior.
This seems to make it very difficult to discovery VAP (or binding) bugs. While I can see a case that leniency makes more successes, I'd try to make it easy to discover bugs and error.
I'm ok breaking people that integrated at this level. They should be aware of the semantic change and this is an easy way to force it.
Given that this KEP has graduated to `stable`, if all the work is completed, could you please update the KEP status in `kep.yaml` to `implemented`
